conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. A Q3 beat against the company's own guide is likely: Klarna beat the top of its revenue guide in Q1 and Q2 and earned $91m adjusted operating income against a $30-50m Q2 guide. But this stock has moved 9-23% on the guide, not the quarter, in 3 of its last 4 prints. The euro is about 4% weaker than when the FY guide was set on 2026-08-18, and CCD II starts on 2026-11-20 in the holiday peak, so FY GMV and revenue could be trimmed again. Against that sit a short of 10% of shares outstanding that is still rising and a stock 61% off its high. Net p_up is 49 on an absolute move of 17 (the confirmed-print median is ~21, the option-implied move 13.1). The findings sum to -0.7, which agrees in sign and roughly in size; neither number is fitted to the other.

expectations.real_bar: Q3 revenue and AOI above the top of the guide, and the FY 2026 GMV, revenue and AOI ranges held, keeping the implied Q4 AOI of about $106-136m intact, despite a euro about 4% weaker than in August and CCD II in force from Nov 20. A third cut to the FY outlook sends the stock down, as the last two did.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY 2026 revenue consensus was $4.42bn before the August cut (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KLAR/earnings-forecasts); no current figure found
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY 2026: GMV $149-151bn, revenue $4.08-4.16bn, TMD $1.62-1.65bn, AOI $280-300m. With H1 AOI at $159m and the Q3 guide at $5-15m, implied Q4 AOI is about $106-136m. With H1 GMV at $70.3bn and the Q3 guide at $35-36bn, implied Q4 GMV is about $43-46bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2003292/000162828026057573/q22026earningsrelease.htm)
next_guide.basis: AOI is likely held, because Q1 and Q2 both beat the AOI guide and give a cushion. Reported GMV and revenue are at risk of landing at or below the low end: EUR/USD fell from about 1.165-1.17 in August to about 1.11-1.12 (a translation hit of roughly $1.0-1.5bn on about 78% non-US Q4 GMV), and CCD II affordability checks start on 2026-11-20. Against that, PayPal called Germany stable to slightly improving and Affirm's US BNPL volumes are growing at more than 30%.

findings.finding: Klarna beat the top of its own revenue guide in each of the last two quarters: Q2 revenue was $1.042bn against a $960m-1.0bn guide and AOI $91m against $30-50m; Q1 revenue was about $1.0bn against $900-980m. The Q3 street revenue of $964-973m sits inside the $940-980m guide, so the same pattern implies revenue of about $990-1,000m (about +2.5% against consensus) and AOI well above the $5-15m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock has not paid for quarterly beats. Q3'25 beat revenue ($903m vs $890m) and fell 9.3%; Q4'25 beat and fell about 22%; Q2'26 beat revenue, EPS and AOI and fell 22.8% on the FY cut. Q1'26 (+20.3%) is the only up print, and that quarter's FY guide was reiterated.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits inside the company's guide, not above it, and has been flat for 60 days, so the street has not modelled the habitual beat of the top end. But a consensus beat is the base case on most releases, and on this name it has been sold three times in four.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 beat versus its Q1 guide: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1928531/klarna-delivers-strong-start-to-2026-with-1bn-revenue-and-68m-adj-operating-profit (a different document, the same company habit).

findings.finding: EUR/USD has fallen from about 1.165-1.17 when Klarna set its FY guide on 2026-08-18 (the 90-day high was 1.1688) to about 1.11-1.12 in early November (2026 low 1.1120 in October; about 1.114 at the end of the first November week). That is about 4% of translation. The August cut already attributed about $600m of GMV to FX. Another ~4% on roughly 78% non-US Q4 GMV of $43-46bn is about $1.0-1.5bn, which would push FY GMV ($149-151bn) and revenue ($4.08-4.16bn) to or below the low end unless volumes offset it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two FY guide cuts (Feb 2026: weak 2026 guide, -22%; Aug 2026: FY GMV/revenue cut, partly for FX, -22.8%) are the two largest down moves on record.
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public, and analysts may have trimmed USD GMV already. But the company has not spoken since August, the September conference did not reaffirm the guide, and the FY ranges in the street's models are the company's. If this were priced, consensus FY revenue would sit visibly at or below $4.08bn; no current FY consensus was found to check. Partly priced.
findings.independence: The euro ended September near 1.135 after its sharpest monthly fall in 14 months: https://tradingeconomics.com/euro-area/currency/news/588042. FX transmission to Klarna's guide is a macro-to-company inference the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: The EU Consumer Credit Directive (CCD II) takes effect on 2026-11-20. It requires affordability checks before Klarna's German 'Kauf auf Rechnung' and 'pay in 30 days' options, possibly asking for income, rent and age, in the middle of the Q4 peak. Germany is Klarna's largest market by volume and was already the cause of the August cut. Klarna's own FAQ says its existing checks already come close to the requirement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: German softness was a named cause of the August FY cut (-22.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: The date has been known for a long time, and previews name it as a holiday-season risk, so it is mostly priced. What is not known is whether management quantifies a Q4 conversion hit in the guide. Klarna says it already runs comparable checks (https://www.klarna.com/international/enterprise/ccd2-faq/), which argues for a small effect.
findings.independence: The Investing.com preview flags the same risk: https://au.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/klarna-earnings-in-focus-as-operating-leverage-faces-test-93CH-4774154

findings.finding: Affirm, Klarna's closest US competitor, reported on 2026-11-05 (fiscal Q1 2027, quarter to September). GMV rose 34% to $14.4bn, its 12th straight quarter above 30%, and Affirm Card GMV rose 117%. Revenue was $1.26bn against a $1.21bn consensus, and early fiscal Q2 trends point to GMV growth in the high-30% range. This points to strong US BNPL demand in Klarna's Q3 and into Q4. Klarna's US GMV was $7.9bn (+27%, 22% of GMV) in Q2, and its US outlook was left unchanged in August.
findings.link: Same product (US point-of-sale instalment credit and BNPL card) and the same merchant channel. Klarna replaced Affirm at Walmart/OnePay. The US is 22% of Klarna GMV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US strength was praised in Q2 (US TMD +126%) and the stock still fell 22.8% on European weakness; this line has not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Affirm reported after Klarna last spoke, and KLAR's 5-day run-up of +1.4% shows no read-through rally. The US is only 22% of GMV, so the read-through is net of the 78% outside the US where the problem sits.
findings.independence: https://www.panabee.com/news/affirm-earnings-q1-2027 (the same Affirm print, a second write-up; one fact).

findings.finding: The same Affirm print showed 30+ day delinquencies up 35bp sequentially to 2.9%, the allowance rising to 6.3% from 5.9% of loans, provisions up 59%, and funding costs up 27bp sequentially, with management expecting rates to stay elevated. Klarna's Q2 provisions were 0.52% of GMV, and the later 2025 US Fair Financing cohorts were inside a 3-4% loss range.
findings.link: Same product and the same US consumer (Klarna US Fair Financing is +82% and 13% of GMV). Funding differs: Klarna is 88% deposit-funded, Affirm uses warehouses and ABS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3'25 the stock fell 9.3% on margin and provision concerns from up-front Fair Financing provisioning (tikr, 2025-11-19); credit has moved this name before.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's credit uptick after Klarna last spoke. Part of a June-to-September delinquency rise is seasonal, and Klarna's book is shorter-duration and mostly European, so the transmission is partial.
findings.independence: Same document as the Affirm volume finding (two lines of one print, counted as one source). Fed hike: https://www.forex.com/en-au/news-and-analysis/eur-usd-q4-2026-outlook-euro-at-a-crossroads-as-fed-ecb-tighten-9-25-2026/

findings.finding: On its Q3 call (about 2026-10-27), PayPal said Germany had been stable and was showing slight improvement, while Italy and France were stable and growing; PayPal Pay Later volume grew about 25%. Klarna's August guide assumed German softness would persist through H2 rather than recover. PayPal also added Amazon Germany and Austria as Pay Later distribution, which competes with Klarna.
findings.link: Same channel and market: PayPal and Klarna are the two largest online checkout and pay-later methods in German e-commerce, and Germany is Klarna's largest market by volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Germany was the named cause of the August cut (-22.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a competitor's commentary about the market Klarna guided down on, given after Klarna last spoke. If it had been read across, KLAR would have rallied off its October lows; it is near $13-14, as in mid-October. It is a proxy, and the Amazon DE distribution win cuts the other way for share.
findings.independence: Zalando's German-heavy Q3 (GMV +6.1% pro forma, FY reaffirmed) points the same way: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/zalando-increases-quarterly-revenue-by-5-percent/2026110375524

findings.finding: Zalando reported on 2026-11-03: Q3 GMV of €4.54bn (+7.5% reported, +6.1% pro forma), adjusted EBIT +10.6%, FY26 guidance reaffirmed in the lower half of 12-17%, and a strong start to the fall/winter season. German-led online fashion demand held through Q3 and into Q4.
findings.link: Same end market (German and European online fashion, Klarna's core European category). Zalando's acceptance of Klarna by market was not verified, so treat this as an end-market link, not a confirmed customer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: European volume commentary set the August reaction (-22.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is not a Klarna document and is not read across in any KLAR preview found. Small, because it is an end-market proxy whose link is not stated with a figure.

findings.finding: Short interest is 38.18M shares (10.1% of shares outstanding, more of the float) at 2026-10-30, up from 31.78M on 2026-08-14 and up in 6 of 7 settlements. Days to cover are 6.6, into a stock 61% below its 52-week high. A held FY guide with a Q3 beat meets a crowded, still-building short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26: guide reiterated, short interest about 27.5M, stock +20.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: A short of this size is itself the market pricing a third cut. The squeeze is a mechanism only if the guide holds, so it is conditional, not free. The skew is flat (+0.2), so options are not pricing a one-sided downside either.
findings.independence: The 2026-10-30 settlement is also at https://massive.com/quote/klar.md (same FINRA data).

findings.finding: Spot is $13.645 against a mean target of $19.24 (25 analysts, 2026-11-16), below the CEO's August purchase price of $14.37 and $6 below the pre-Q2 close of $19.51. Target cuts have already run (UBS to Neutral and $16, TD Cowen $18 to $16 about 2026-10-06), and the 20-day run-up is only +4.3%. The market's bar has been reset low since August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26 came in after a -22% Feb print with the stock near lows and rose 20.3%; Q2'26 came in after a run to about $20 and fell 22.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by definition it is the market's expectation. The finding is that the bar is low relative to targets and to the last pre-print level, which favours an upside asymmetry only if the guide holds.

findings.finding: In 3 of the last 4 confirmed prints the stock fell sharply despite beating the quarter (Nov 2025 -9.3%, Feb 2026 about -22%, Aug 2026 -22.8%). The direction each time was set by forward guidance or profitability, and the one up print (May 2026 +20.3%) reiterated FY. The baseline's 8-event history mixes in non-earnings 6-Ks; the confirmed-print median absolute move is about 21%.
findings.why_not_priced: History is not a forecast. The finding is that the reaction function has punished the guide more often than it rewarded the beat. The options price a 13% move, well below the realised ~21% median.
findings.independence: Q3'25 -9.3%: https://www.tikr.com/blog/klarna-stock-sinks-over-9-despite-beating-consensus-estimates-in-q3. Aug 2026 -22.81% and May 2026 +20.31% are in the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: A Form 4 shows CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski bought 692,506 shares on 2026-08-26 at a weighted $14.3669 (about $9.95m), raising his holding to more than 25.3M shares. The stock now trades about 5% below that price. Separately, he was granted options on 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-01 (reported late on 2026-10-30), which is compensation and not a signal.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and three months old, so it is largely priced. An insider buying after a guide cut and before the next print is weak evidence the CEO did not expect a further deterioration.
findings.independence: Option grant Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2003292/000209710726000005/primary_doc.xml. The Flat Capital purchase is the same transaction: https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/flat-capital-acquires-an-additional-692506-shares-in-klarna-for-sek-95-million

findings.finding: The only management statement after the 2026-08-18 call found is CFO Neglén at Goldman Sachs Communacopia on 2026-09-09. He did not reaffirm the FY guide, said guidance 'will be updated quarterly based on real-time transaction data', repeated that German online sales underperformed, and said the US leads with 30M users and Walmart and Apple driving high-ticket financing.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and silence is weak evidence. Not reaffirming two months before FX moved further leaves the guide open to revision; a company confident in the range would usually say 'on track'.

findings.finding: The Fed hiked in September 2026 (its first hike since 2023) and the ECB is also tightening. Klarna's funding cost was $171m, 0.47% of GMV, in Q2, with deposits at 88% of funding ($11.7bn, down from $13.0bn at December 2025). Higher deposit and benchmark rates pressure TMD and the fair-value adjustments on loans sold in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25 TMD missed guidance (faster lending growth) and the stock fell about 22%.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate moves are public, and the Q3 TMD guide ($340-360m) may already include them. Transmission to Klarna is not confirmed by the company, so this is a small proxy.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-12 Klarna named Chris Koegel, Robinhood's VP and Head of Corporate Finance and IR, as CFO from 2027-01-01, ending the CFO vacancy UBS flagged in August. The 6-K says nothing about Q3 or guidance, and the stock fell 5.64% that day for a reason not stated.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement is public and was already traded on 11-12 (down). A US-listed-fintech IR veteran may matter for credibility on the call. Small.

findings.finding: The FY AOI guide of $280-300m, less H1 AOI of $159m and the Q3 guide of $5-15m, implies Q4 AOI of about $106-136m, the largest quarter by far. Management made that conditional on PSP integrations and large signed merchants going live before peak, and called Q4 'our strongest transaction margin quarter'. Klarna missed its own TMD guide in Q4 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25 TMD missed its guide and the stock fell about 22% (Feb 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but the Q4 guide arrives tomorrow, and any slip of launches or merchant go-lives shows up as a Q4 AOI guide below the implied $106-136m. The Q3 AOI beat (finding 1) can offset this inside the FY range.

findings.finding: Pomerantz Law Firm issued an investor alert on 2026-09-22 about possible claims for Klarna investors (a securities-litigation investigation after the August drop).
findings.why_not_priced: Routine plaintiff-firm alert, public, near zero.

findings.finding: Unusually heavy bearish put activity in KLAR was reported around 2026-11-12, and front-expiry put/call open interest is 1.43 (baseline). Some participants have bought downside into the print, but the 25-delta skew is flat at +0.2 vol pts.
findings.why_not_priced: Options flow is price, so this is already in the implied move. The flat skew says the market as a whole is not leaning down.

CCD II's actual effect on Klarna's German and EU conversion over Black Friday and the holiday peak will only be visible in Q4 results (Feb 2027), beyond whatever the Q4 guide says.

baseline_tension: The evidence is close to balanced, as is the baseline (skew +0.2, lean balanced). Against it are the crowded and rising short (a reason to shrink negatives) and the low bar after a 61% drawdown. With it are the name's habit of falling on the guide and the FX and CCD II pressure on the FY ranges.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold beats in 3 of 4 prints): Q3 beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5; p_up moved toward 50 (48 to 49).

Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks negatives; SI 10.1% of shares outstanding and rising, DTC 6.6): FX guide finding -1.5 to -1.2, CCD II -0.8 to -0.6, Q4 back-end-loading -1.0 to -0.8, reaction-history -0.8 to -0.6.
Lesson 8 and the reaction-history rebuild (the baseline's 8 events mix in non-earnings 6-Ks; the confirmed-print median is ~21%): abs_move_pct raised from 15 to 17.

print_vs_bar_pct moved from +2.0 to +2.5 after rechecking that Klarna beat the top of its revenue guide in both Q1 and Q2 (lesson 6: the bar is sourced to the company guide and three agreeing estimates).
Lesson 5 (proxies small, never dropped): the PayPal, Zalando, Affirm and Fed findings left at their small draft sizes.
